author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Rhode Island Department of Health is asking anyone who had direct contact with a bat at Roger Williams Park Zoo on or before August 24 to contact the state. The bat was seen near the zoo’s water-play area and was reported to health officials on Friday, September 11. A zoo veterinarian assessed the episode as presenting a low risk of human exposure.

The animal was safely discarded before it could be tested for rabies, and officials said the zoo had received no earlier reports involving the bat. Because testing was not possible, the department is using the public notice to identify any person who may have touched the animal or had another form of direct contact that should be evaluated.

RIDOH said potentially exposed visitors should call its Center for Acute Infectious Disease Epidemiology at 401-222-2577 on weekdays or 401-276-8046 after hours. The department notes that rabies can be prevented with post-exposure vaccination when treatment begins before symptoms appear. The request is limited to people with possible direct contact; officials did not characterize ordinary zoo attendance as an exposure.
dek: Health officials say the chance of human exposure was low, but anyone who touched the bat at Roger Williams Park Zoo should call the state.
headline: Rhode Island seeks visitors who contacted bat at Providence zoo
